summary_html: A **law-enforcement agency** encounters suspected maltreatment (e.g., during a domestic call or arrest) and **refers** to CPS. Federal child-abuse infrastructure promotes coordinated investigations via Children’s Advocacy Centers.
authority_html:
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — support for multidisciplinary teams and CAC protocols; coordination with CPS  
- **ASFA/SSA IV-E** — court findings and reasonable-efforts determinations later constrain downstream actions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: A fifteen-year-old in DCF custody was in custody for Miranda purposes when questioned by police at his foster home, so the resulting statements were suppressed and the trial court judgment reversed.
key_cases.relevance: E.W. governs police questioning of a child in state custody and the role of an 'independent interested adult' when the foster parent is the adult present.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the juvenile was in custody, and therefore reverse the trial court judgment.

key_cases.holding: The delinquency adjudication was reversed and the juvenile's statements suppressed because, under Chapter I, Article 10 of the Vermont Constitution, a juvenile may waive counsel and the privilege against self-incrimination only after an opportunity to consult privately with an informed adult who is independent of the prosecution, and the state-contracted group-home director was not such an adult.
key_cases.relevance: E.T.C. is the foundational Vermont rule governing police contact with children, requiring an independent interested adult before any juvenile waiver, and it arose from state troopers questioning children who were in SRS custody in a state-contracted group home.
key_cases.quote: Although our prior cases apply only to waivers in court, we now hold that the same principles apply to police interrogation of juvenile suspects.

search_keywords: Vermont Department for Children and Families

state_agency.name: Vermont Department for Children and Families, Family Services Division

mandatory_reporters: Health care providers, including physicians, surgeons, osteopaths, chiropractors, physician assistants, resident physicians, interns, hospital administrators, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, medical examiners, emergency medical personnel, dentists, psychologists, and pharmacists — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(1)

School district and approved or recognized independent school employees, and contracted student-services providers, including superintendents, headmasters, teachers, student teachers, school librarians, principals, and guidance counselors — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(2)
Agency of Human Services employees, contractors, and grantees who have contact with clients — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(7)
Camp owners (“camp” includes any residential or nonresidential recreational program, 33 V.S.A. § 4913(b)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(9)
Members of the clergy, except information received while acting as a spiritual advisor in a confidential communication (33 V.S.A. § 4913(j)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(12)
Employees of the Office of the Child, Youth, and Family Advocate — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(13)
reporting_details: Vermont is not a universal-reporting state: the 13 categories of mandated reporters listed in 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a) must report to DCF within 24 hours of the time the information was first received or observed, and any other concerned person may report voluntarily (33 V.S.A. § 4913(c), (e)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 72 hours to begin an assessment or investigation
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the report, once accepted as a valid allegation and there is sufficient information to proceed
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The Commissioner may waive the 72-hour requirement only when necessary to locate the child or to ensure the safety of the child or social worker (33 V.S.A. § 4915(b)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days (assessment track); no statutory deadline (investigation track)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An assessment may be extended only upon written justification by the Department and not beyond 60 days total (33 V.S.A. § 4915a(b)); Vermont sets no completion deadline for the investigation track (33 V.S.A. § 4915b).
